# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 10 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_010_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 2

**1** The tower was being built upon a great square rock. This rock was older than the world itself, and the tower was founded upon it. **2** The rock and its gate were newly cut. Six young men, strong and all alike in appearance, were building the tower. **3** Many thousands of other men were bringing stones for the construction — some from the sea, others from dry land. **4** The stones from the sea were polished and square; those from dry land varied — some were square, some round, some smooth, some rough. Some of the rough ones fit into the building; others did not fit at all. **5** The six young men were overseeing the whole operation. I stood and watched the progress of the building. **6** I observed that the tower was rising in a solid and beautiful form. Seven women stood encircling the tower. The first was named Faith; the second Self-control; the third Power; the fourth Patience; the fifth Simplicity; the sixth Innocence; the seventh Purity. **7** Of all these, the first was the strongest — girded and acting in a powerful way. The others, linking hands with each other, danced in a circle around the tower.

---

*LOGOS note: The seven virtues here are more commonly translated Faith, Continence/Self-control, Power, Patience, Simplicity, Innocence, Purity — matching the seven spirits/virtues of the Shepherd's theological system.*
